record.original_question: Show that the CG and Lanczos algorithms do or do not behave similarly in finite precision arithmetic when used to solve a symmetric positive definite linear system. This will, of course, depend on the implementation of each method, so use standard good implementations of both.

evidence.quote: Show that the CG and Lanczos algorithms do or do not behave similarly in finite precision arithmetic when used to solve a symmetric positive definite linear system. This will, of course, depend on the implementation of each method, so use standard good implementations of both.

artifact.category_tag: Conjugate Gradient and Lanczos methods in finite precision
artifact.status_search_result: The question is an open-ended exercise asking for a comparative analysis of CG and Lanczos in finite precision. The general topic has been studied extensively (notably by Paige, Greenbaum, Strakoš, Meurant, and others), who showed that finite-precision CG behaves like exact CG applied to a larger matrix with clustered eigenvalues, and that loss of orthogonality and delay of convergence occur in closely related ways for CG and Lanczos. However, as stated the prompt is a pedagogical/research exercise rather than a precisely formulated conjecture with a definitive solved/open status, so its status is best regarded as unknown.

status_evidence.title: Behavior of slightly perturbed Lanczos and conjugate-gradient recurrences
status_evidence.snippet: Greenbaum (1989) shows that finite precision CG and Lanczos recurrences can be analyzed via an exact computation on a nearby matrix with clustered eigenvalues.
status_evidence.claim: Foundational analysis relating finite-precision CG and Lanczos behavior.

status_evidence.title: Predicting the behavior of finite precision Lanczos and conjugate gradient computations
status_evidence.snippet: Greenbaum and Strakoš analyze how finite-precision CG and Lanczos iterations track exact iterations on enlarged systems.
status_evidence.claim: Standard reference comparing CG and Lanczos in finite precision.
